'''Grace Afua Bediako'''  is a Ghanaian statistician and the former head of the [[Ghana Statistical Service]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NDPC urges political parties to adopt 40 year development plan|url=https://www.newsghana.com.gh/ndpc-urges-political-parties-to-adopt-40-year-development-plan/|website=News Ghana|accessdate=29 August 2016}}</ref> She was formerly a member of the [[National Development Planning Commission (NDPC)]].<ref name=Akinyi>{{cite web|last1=Akinyi|first1=Merab|title=Grace Bediako|url=http://africainequalities.org/panel/grace-bediako/|website=Portal on African Inequalities and Structural Transformation|publisher=African Inequalities|accessdate=29 August 2016|date=2014-02-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=STATS BOSS UNDER FIRE …GSS workers angry at Grace Bediako|url=http://www.todaygh.com/stats-boss-under-fire-gss-workers-angry-at-grace-bediako/|website=Today online|accessdate=29 August 2016|archive-date=27 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200127083536/http://www.todaygh.com/stats-boss-under-fire-gss-workers-angry-at-grace-bediako/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==
Bediako had her secondary education at [[Achimota School]], and earned her first degree in Economics and Statistics from the [[University of Ghana]]. She earned a PhD degree in Demography from the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. Prior to earning her doctorate degree in 1988, she acquired a diploma in Population Studies from the Regional Institute for Population Studies, [[Legon]], as well as a Postgraduate Certificate in Survey Sampling from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=GFA>{{cite web|title=Ghanaian Female Achievers|url=http://femaleachievers.org/dir_profile_details.cfm?dowdirID=633&prof_categoryid=81&category_id=1|website=|publisher=Ministry of Women and Children Affairs|date=17 November 2012|accessdate=29 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911214305/http://femaleachievers.org/dir_profile_details.cfm?dowdirID=633&prof_categoryid=81&category_id=1|archive-date=11 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=Akinyi />

==Career==
Grace Bediako started her career as a government statistician. She was appointed to be the head of the Ghana Statistical Service, and served from June 2004 to June 2012.<ref name=Akinyi /> Prior to her career with the [[Government of Ghana]], she was Chief of Demographic Statistics Section, [[United Nations Statistics Division]] from 2000 to 2004.<ref name=GFA /> She is currently the consultant to the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) and also a board member for Savannah Accelerated Development Authority (SADA), Coastal Development Authority <ref>{{cite web|title=President reconstitutes SADA Boar|url=http://www.presidency.gov.gh/node/535|website=The Presidency Republic of Ghana|accessdate=29 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911090238/http://www.presidency.gov.gh/node/535|archive-date=11 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Let's support the 40-year dev't plan - Grace Bediako|url=http://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Let-s-support-the-40-year-dev-t-plan-Grace-Bediako-373367|website=Ghanaweb|accessdate=29 August 2016|archive-date=18 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160918195544/http://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Let-s-support-the-40-year-dev-t-plan-Grace-Bediako-373367|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ghanalive.tv/2015/08/06/grace-bediako-urged-ghanaians-to-support-40-year-devt-plan/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917012331/http://www.ghanalive.tv/2015/08/06/grace-bediako-urged-ghanaians-to-support-40-year-devt-plan/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=September 17, 2016|title=Grace Bediako urged Ghanaians to support 40-year Dev't plan|last=Christie|first=Marian|date=2015-08-06|website=Ghana Live TV|access-date=2016-08-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dr Grace Bediako|url=https://www.coda.gov.gh/profile/1.13479594|website=Ghanaweb|accessdate=27 November 2020}}</ref> and a representative of the Internal Audit Agency serving as a member of the Audit Committee of the Ghana Science Association <ref>http://www.ghanascience.gov.gh/</ref>.

==Awards==
Bediako received the President's award of the [[Order of the Volta]] for Public Service in 2008.<ref name=Akinyi />
She is also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.isi-web.org/index.php/about-isi/who-is-isi/members/indivual|title=Individual members|publisher=International Statistical Institute|accessdate=2017-11-23|archive-date=2017-07-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729010059/https://www.isi-web.org/index.php/about-isi/who-is-isi/members/indivual|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Works and publications==
Bediako compiled and published the Annual Economic Survey<ref name=GFA /> She is also responsible for the production of three major [[United Nations]] methodological reports: ''Handbook for Producing a National Statistical Reports on Women and Men'', ''Technical Report on Collecting Economic Characteristics in Population and Housing Censuses'', and ''Trial International Classification for Time-use Activities''.<ref name=Akinyi />

As a government statistician, she led numerous surveys, including the Ghana Living Standards Survey, 2005/06; Crime Victimization Survey, 2009; and National Population and Housing Census, 2010. She also formulated the five-year Ghana Statistics Development Plan, which sought to strengthen the institutional and human resource capacity of the different ministries,  departments and agencies with linkages as well as sources of data for the compilation of national statistics.<ref name=GFA />
